answers.value: Both statements are incorrect: a private member is any MP who is not a Minister (election vs nomination is irrelevant), and private member's bills have been passed before — fourteen of them
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong on the definition: a 'private member' is simply any Member of Parliament who is not a Minister. Elected backbenchers are private members; whether an MP is elected or nominated by the President has nothing to do with it. Statement 2 is wrong on the history: fourteen private member's bills have been passed by Parliament since independence, the last being the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Bill, so no recent passage could be 'the first time in its history'. Since neither holds, the answer is D.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong because the Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age culture that did not know iron (and did know gold and silver)
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Rigveda refers to body armour (varman) and helmet (sipra) in warfare, and Harappan sites have yielded no evidence of either. Statement 2 is the false one and it fails twice over — the Indus Valley Civilization was a Chalcolithic/Bronze Age culture that had no knowledge of iron, and it certainly did know gold and silver (ornaments and vessels are common finds). Statement 3 is correct at textbook level: the horse is central to Rigvedic life (the ashva, the chariot, the ashvamedha) while the Harappan seals depict the bull, elephant, rhinoceros, tiger and buffalo but never the horse. Note that a few disputed horse-bone finds at Surkotada have been argued for, but the standard position is that the Harappans were not familiar with the animal. With statement 2 excluded, only C survives.

answers.value: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills that workers already acquired informally, through traditional/on-the-job channels rather than through formal training
answers.reasoning: The defining feature of 'Recognition of Prior Learning' is in its name: it assesses and certifies competencies a person has ALREADY picked up outside any formal training system, aligning that unregulated workforce to the National Skills Qualifications Framework. Option A is the only one that names learning acquired 'through traditional channels', and the construction sector has been the largest and most publicised cohort under it. Option D is the trap and it contradicts the word 'prior': people who are trainees under a skill development programme are being trained now and are certified on that training, which is not prior learning at all. Runner-up: D. It would win if the setter treated RPL simply as the certification arm of the National Skill Development Programme and considered option A's restriction to construction workers too narrow to be the general description — RPL is in fact run across many sectors, not only construction.

answers.value: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, which sits at the junction of the two hill ranges and forms the corridor linking the Western Ghats/Nilgiri landscape to the Eastern Ghats
answers.reasoning: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve in Erode district of Tamil Nadu lies exactly where the Eastern Ghats meet the Western Ghats, and it is the critical elephant and tiger corridor connecting the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve landscape in the west with the Eastern Ghats to the east. The other three are all confined to one range: Nallamala Forest and Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve are wholly in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh, and Nagarhole National Park is wholly within the Western Ghats in Karnataka, so none of them can be a link between the two.

answers.value: Absence of privileges — equality means no special or hereditary advantages for any class of persons
answers.reasoning: Equality in political theory means the absence of special privilege: no person or class enjoys advantages denied to others merely by birth, rank or status. That is precisely what Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution do in abolishing untouchability and titles. Restraints (B) belong to the discussion of liberty, not equality, and even liberty is not the absence of all restraint. Competition (C) is compatible with equality — equality of opportunity presupposes competition on equal terms. Ideology (D) is unrelated.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct: TRAFFIC is a joint programme of WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau, but its stated mission on wildlife trade is accurately described
answers.reasoning: TRAFFIC is a wildlife trade monitoring network set up as a strategic alliance of WWF and IUCN. It is not a bureau under the United Nations Environment Programme, and it is not a UN body at all, so statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 reproduces TRAFFIC's own stated mission — to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature — and is correct. Hence B.

answers.value: Participation of workers in the management of industries (Article 43A), inserted into Part IV by the 42nd Amendment, 1976
answers.reasoning: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added three new Directive Principles: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers in the management of industries) and Article 48A (protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife). Of the four options only 'participation of workers in the management of industries' is among them. The other three are all part of the original 1950 text — equal pay for equal work is Article 39(d), the right to work, education and public assistance is Article 41, and securing a living wage and humane conditions of work is Article 43.

answers.value: Rights are claims of the citizens against the State
answers.reasoning: A right is a claim that the individual holds and that the State is bound to recognise and enforce; the direction of the claim runs from citizen to State, which is why Fundamental Rights are enforceable against the State under Article 32. Option A reverses the direction — the State has powers and the citizen has duties, not the other way round. Option B is too narrow, since rights exist as moral and legal claims whether or not a written constitution enumerates them. Option D describes privilege, which is the opposite of a right: rights belong to all citizens equally.

answers.value: The World Economic Forum publishes the Global Gender Gap Index and Report
answers.reasoning: The Global Gender Gap Index has been published annually by the World Economic Forum since 2006, ranking countries on gender parity across four sub-indices: economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. The UN Human Rights Council, UN Women and the WHO do not produce it. UNDP separately publishes the Gender Inequality Index, which is a different measure and a common source of confusion.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct: Smart India Hackathon is a nationwide contest to find digital technology solutions to problems posed by government ministries
answers.reasoning: Smart India Hackathon 2017 was a product-development competition in which student teams built digital solutions to problem statements submitted by central ministries and departments, so statement 2 is correct. It is a hackathon, not a centrally sponsored scheme, and it has nothing to do with converting cities into Smart Cities — that is the separate Smart Cities Mission — so statement 1 is incorrect. Nor is it a programme for making all financial transactions digital, which conflates it with the Digital India and cashless-economy push, so statement 3 is incorrect.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct: the MPC fixes the policy repo rate, but it has six members and is chaired by the RBI Governor, not twelve members under the Finance Minister
answers.reasoning: The Monetary Policy Committee, constituted under the amended RBI Act, is charged with determining the policy repo rate required to achieve the inflation target, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong on both counts: the MPC has six members — the Governor, a Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, an officer nominated by the Central Board, and three external members appointed by the Government — and the external members hold office for four years, so it is not reconstituted every year. Statement 3 is wrong because the Governor of the RBI is the ex officio chairperson and holds the casting vote in a tie; the Union Finance Minister is not a member at all.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 fails because the pung drum, not just cymbals, is central to Sankirtana
answers.reasoning: Manipuri Sankirtana, inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, is a performing art combining singing, drumming and dancing in Vaishnava temples, so statement 1 is correct, and it narrates the lives and deeds of Krishna, so statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is the false one: the performance is led by drummers playing the pung (the Manipuri barrel drum), alongside cymbals (kartal) and singer-dancers, so cymbals are plainly not the only instruments used.

answers.value: Alexander Read and Thomas Munro introduced the Ryotwari Settlement; Cornwallis is associated with the Permanent Settlement instead
answers.reasoning: The Ryotwari system, in which revenue was settled directly with the individual cultivator (ryot) without any intermediary zamindar, was first worked out by Captain Alexander Read in the Baramahal region after 1792 and then developed and extended across the Madras Presidency by Thomas Munro, who became Governor of Madras. Lord Cornwallis is associated with the entirely different Permanent Settlement of 1793 in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, which created a hereditary class of zamindars as revenue proprietors. So only 2 and 3 belong, giving C.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are advantages; statement 2 is false because heavy metals such as cadmium and lead are not biodegradable and cannot be completely removed by microorganisms
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct and is the textbook definition: bioremediation works by stimulating and enhancing the natural biodegradation that microorganisms already carry out, typically by supplying oxygen or nutrients. Statement 3 is correct — genetically engineered organisms have been designed for the purpose, the classic instance being Ananda Chakrabarty's oil-degrading 'superbug'. Statement 2 is false: heavy metals are elements and cannot be broken down at all. Microbes may change a metal's oxidation state or immobilise it, but nothing is destroyed, so the claim that 'any contaminant with heavy metals... can be readily and completely treated' is wrong both in its absoluteness and in its chemistry.

answers.value: A system of tribunals (Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation) for settling industrial disputes, together with a ban on strikes
answers.reasoning: The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 set up machinery for compulsory settlement of industrial disputes — Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation — and simultaneously curbed the right to strike, prohibiting strikes in public utility services without prior notice and outlawing strikes that had objects other than the furtherance of a trade dispute. That combination of an adjudicatory apparatus plus restriction on strikes is what option D describes. It gave nothing to workers by way of participation in management (A), conferred no arbitrary powers on employers as such (B), and involved no British court sitting in judgement over Indian disputes (C).

answers.value: Democratic decentralisation — the transfer of powers, functions and finances to elected local bodies
answers.reasoning: Local self-government means that people at the village, block, district and municipal level elect their own bodies and exercise real powers, functions and finances devolved to them, which is exactly what 'democratic decentralisation' denotes, and is the phrase the Balwantrai Mehta Committee itself used. It is not federalism (A), because India's federal division is only between the Union and the States and the third tier is created by State law under the 73rd and 74th Amendments. It is not mere administrative delegation (C), because delegated officials remain accountable upward while panchayats are elected and accountable to the people. And it is not direct democracy (D), since panchayats govern through elected representatives, the gram sabha notwithstanding.

answers.value: The Directive Principles operate on both the legislative and the executive functions, because 'State' in Part IV covers both and Article 37 makes them fundamental in the governance of the country
answers.reasoning: Article 37 declares that the Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and that it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. 'State' here carries the Article 12 meaning and so takes in both the legislature and the executive, and the phrase 'governance of the country' extends beyond law-making to administration. The Principles therefore act as instructions that circumscribe how both functions may be exercised, even though Article 37 makes them non-justiciable, which is why the courts read them as guiding the reasonableness of executive action and the construction of statutes. Runner-up: D. It would win if the setter took the strict view that only a justiciable provision can be a 'limitation' — on that reading Fundamental Rights are the limitations on State power and the Directive Principles are positive obligations that limit nothing, so neither statement would hold. A narrower runner-up is A, if the setter had fastened on Article 37's literal words 'in making laws' and confined the Principles to the legislative function alone. [Answer corrected to D from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached C. The reasoning above argues for C and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: The European Union's Digital Single Market Strategy
answers.reasoning: The Digital Single Market Strategy was adopted by the European Commission in 2015 to remove regulatory barriers between the EU's national online markets and turn them into a single market — covering matters such as ending mobile roaming charges, portability of digital content, and harmonised e-commerce and data protection rules. The very notion of a 'single market' is EU vocabulary, deriving from its internal market, and has no counterpart in ASEAN, BRICS or the G20, none of which is a customs-union style single market.

answers.value: Chandipur beach in Odisha, where the very gentle gradient lets the low tide withdraw the sea several kilometres and expose the sea floor twice a day
answers.reasoning: Chandipur, on the Bay of Bengal in the Balasore district of Odisha, is famous for exactly this: the extremely shallow gradient of the shore means that at low tide the water retreats up to about five kilometres, so visitors can walk out on the exposed sea bed, and the sea returns at high tide, twice each day. The phenomenon has earned it the name 'the hide-and-seek beach'. Bhavnagar, Bheemunipatnam and Nagapattinam have no such characteristic.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct: benami property is liable to confiscation; an unaware owner is a defining mark of a benami transaction rather than an exemption, and the Act does provide an appellate mechanism
answers.reasoning: Statement 2 is correct: the Act empowers the Central Government to confiscate property held benami, and without payment of compensation. Statement 1 inverts the law — a transaction in which the owner of the property is not aware of, or denies knowledge of, the ownership is itself listed in the statutory definition of a benami transaction, so being unaware makes it benami rather than exempting it. Statement 3 is wrong twice over: the amended Act establishes four authorities — the Initiating Officer, the Approving Authority, the Administrator and the Adjudicating Authority — and it expressly provides an Appellate Tribunal, with a further appeal to the High Court. Hence only 2 stands.

answers.value: Consequences 1 and 3 follow — pollination is impaired and predators/parasitoids that depend on butterflies and their larvae decline; a rise in fungal infection of crops does not follow
answers.reasoning: Butterflies are important pollinators for many flowering plants, so a crash in their numbers would adversely affect pollination, making statement 1 correct. Butterflies and especially their caterpillars are a major food resource for insectivorous birds and for spiders, and are the hosts on which many parasitoid wasps depend to complete their life cycle, so losing them would pull down those populations too, making statement 3 correct. Statement 2 does not follow: butterflies neither cause nor suppress fungal disease in plants, and there is no mechanism by which their disappearance would produce a drastic increase in fungal infections of cultivated crops.

answers.value: Limitations 2 and 3 are real; statement 1 is false because algae can be cultivated on land in open ponds and photobioreactors, not only in the sea
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is plainly wrong — algal biofuel cultivation is done in land-based open raceway ponds and in closed photobioreactors, and can even use wastewater or saline water on non-arable land, so it is in no way restricted to the seas. Statement 2 is a genuine limitation for developing countries: designing, engineering and commissioning an algal biofuel facility demands considerable technical expertise that such countries may have to import. Statement 3 is also a genuine limitation: economic viability requires very large facilities, whose demands on land and water and whose effects on surrounding ecosystems and communities raise ecological and social objections. So 2 and 3 only.

answers.value: Only objectives 1 and 2 belong to the National Nutrition Mission — awareness among pregnant women and lactating mothers, and reduction of anaemia; promoting millets/unpolished rice and poultry eggs are not among its objectives
answers.reasoning: The National Nutrition Mission is built around measurable nutrition outcomes — reducing stunting, under-nutrition, low birth weight and anaemia — delivered through convergence, ICT-based monitoring and an awareness and behaviour-change campaign aimed at pregnant women, lactating mothers and adolescent girls. Statements 1 and 2 fall squarely within that mandate. Statements 3 and 4 prescribe particular foods, and the Mission does not set targets for promoting millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice, nor for promoting poultry eggs; those belong to food-production and mid-day-meal debates rather than to the Mission's own objectives. Runner-up: B. It would win if the setter counted the Mission's dietary-diversification and food-fortification messaging as amounting to an objective of promoting millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice, in which case statement 3 would be admitted and the answer would become 1, 2 and 3 only.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct: N.M. Lokhande pioneered labour organisation in India, while the Factories Act of 1881 dealt with child labour and machinery safety, not wages or trade unions
answers.reasoning: The first Indian Factories Act of 1881 addressed the employment of children — prohibiting work by children under seven, limiting the hours of those aged seven to twelve, and requiring dangerous machinery to be fenced. It said nothing about fixing the wages of industrial workers and nothing about permitting trade unions, which came only much later with the Trade Unions Act of 1926, so statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 is correct: Narayan Meghaji Lokhande organised the Bombay Mill-Hands Association in 1884, generally regarded as the first labour association in India, and is rightly called a pioneer of the labour movement in British India.

answers.value: All three are recognised geological storage sites for carbon dioxide — abandoned coal seams, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, and deep saline formations
answers.reasoning: All three are standard options in carbon capture and storage. Unmineable or abandoned coal seams can adsorb carbon dioxide onto the coal, and injecting it can simultaneously displace methane (enhanced coal bed methane recovery). Depleted oil and gas reservoirs are among the most attractive sites because they demonstrably held hydrocarbons under an impermeable cap rock for geological time, so their sealing capacity is proven, and injection can be combined with enhanced oil recovery. Deep saline formations are the largest reservoir of all by volume, holding brine unfit for use, where carbon dioxide is trapped structurally and eventually dissolves and mineralises. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

answers.value: The Butler Committee (Indian States Committee, 1927) was appointed to examine the relationship between the Paramount Power and the Indian princely States
answers.reasoning: The Indian States Committee of 1927, chaired by Sir Harcourt Butler, was appointed to inquire into the relationship between the Paramount Power and the Indian (princely) States and to recommend how that relationship should be conducted; it reported in 1929. Option D is the only one that touches the princely States at all. Option A describes the concern of the constitutional reform debates and later the Government of India Act, 1935; option B relates to the India Office and not to Butler; option C describes press legislation such as the Vernacular Press Act. Note the stem's phrase 'Government of India' is a loose rendering of the Crown as Paramount Power, but D remains the intended and only defensible answer.

answers.value: Domestic Content Requirement refers to the rule requiring solar power developers to use domestically manufactured cells and modules under India's solar mission
answers.reasoning: Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) clauses in the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission obliged selected solar developers to source solar cells and modules manufactured in India. The United States challenged these clauses at the WTO as discriminatory against imported equipment, and the dispute panel and Appellate Body ruled against India in 2016, which is why the term was repeatedly in the news. The other options relate to broadcasting policy, agricultural export standards and higher-education FDI, none of which uses this term.

answers.value: Both statements are wrong: the Nuclear Security Summits were a US-initiated process outside the UN, and the International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent expert group, not an IAEA organ
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Nuclear Security Summits (Washington 2010, Seoul 2012, The Hague 2014, Washington 2016) were launched on the initiative of the United States and ran as a stand-alone leaders' process, not under the aegis of the United Nations. Statement 2 is incorrect: the International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent group of arms-control and non-proliferation experts, hosted at Princeton University, and has no institutional link to the International Atomic Energy Agency. With both statements false the answer is D.

answers.value: State government employees who join service after their own State notifies the scheme are covered by the NPS
answers.reasoning: The National Pension System was extended to State government employees State by State, each State applying it to employees recruited after the date of its own notification, so option C is correct. Option A is wrong because Non-Resident Indians may also join NPS, not only resident citizens. Option B is wrong because the entry age band is 18 to 60 years (later widened), not 21 to 55. Option D is wrong on two counts: the mandatory central-government coverage applies to those joining on or after 1 January 2004, and personnel of the Armed Forces are expressly excluded from it.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct: the Rangeet rises in Sikkim and is a tributary of the Teesta; the Teesta does not share the Brahmaputra's source and does not reach the Bay of Bengal directly
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Teesta rises from the Tso Lhamo lake and Zemu glacier area in North Sikkim, whereas the Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) rises from the Chemayungdung/Angsi glacier region near Mansarovar in Tibet, so their sources are quite different. Statement 2 is correct: the Rangeet (Rangit) rises in western Sikkim and joins the Teesta near Melli on the Sikkim-West Bengal border. Statement 3 is incorrect: after entering Bangladesh the Teesta joins the Brahmaputra/Jamuna near Chilmari, so it is a tributary and does not itself debouch into the Bay of Bengal. Only statement 2 stands, giving B.

answers.value: Both statements are correct: Zika is spread in the tropics by Aedes aegypti, the dengue vector, and sexual transmission of Zika is documented
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: in tropical regions the principal vector of Zika virus is Aedes aegypti, the same day-biting mosquito that transmits dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever. Statement 2 is also correct: Zika is unusual among mosquito-borne flaviviruses in that it persists in semen and can be transmitted sexually, which is why health advisories issued during the 2015-16 outbreak covered sexual as well as vector transmission. Both being true, the answer is C.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct: the BIS Standard Mark is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes, while AGMARK is issued by India's Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, not by the FAO
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: pneumatic tyres and tubes for motor vehicles fall under the list of products for which BIS certification (the ISI mark) is compulsory, on safety grounds. Statement 2 is incorrect: AGMARK is a certification mark for agricultural produce issued under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection in the Union Ministry of Agriculture; the Food and Agriculture Organisation is a UN body and issues no such national mark. Hence A.

answers.value: Both statements are correct: eNAM is a pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities, and it is designed to give farmers access to a nationwide market with quality-linked prices
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the National Agriculture Market (eNAM) is precisely a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing APMC mandis into a single online market. Statement 2 is also correct and is the scheme's central promise: by combining online bidding across a nationwide pool of buyers with assaying facilities at the mandi, it aims to give the farmer a wider market and a price that reflects the assessed quality of the produce rather than a local buyer's estimate. The runner-up is B (2 only), which would win if 'advantage' is read strictly, since statement 1 is a description of what the scheme IS rather than a benefit it delivers; for B to be correct the examiner would have to be enforcing that feature-versus-benefit distinction, which UPSC often does not.

answers.value: Both statements are correct: the National IPR Policy affirms India's commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and TRIPS, and DIPP is the nodal agency for intellectual property in India
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the National Intellectual Property Rights Policy, 2016 explicitly reaffirms India's commitment to the Doha Development Round declaration on TRIPS and public health, and states that India's IP regime is fully TRIPS-compliant. Statement 2 is correct as the policy itself frames it: the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion was designated the nodal department to coordinate, guide and oversee implementation of the policy, and administration of the Copyright Act was moved to DIPP in 2016 to consolidate IP under one department. The runner-up is A (1 only), which would win if 'regulating' is read strictly, because DIPP is not the regulator for every IP right: plant varieties sit with the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority under the Agriculture Ministry, and semiconductor layout designs with MeitY.

answers.value: All three - gharial, Indian wild ass and wild buffalo - are Schedule I animals that may not be hunted except as the Act allows
answers.reasoning: Section 9 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 prohibits hunting of animals specified in the Schedules, subject only to the narrow exceptions in sections 11 and 12 (danger to human life, disease, education and scientific research, and the like). The gharial, the Indian wild ass of the Rann of Kutch and the wild buffalo are all listed in Schedule I, which carries the highest level of protection and the severest penalties. Since all three are covered, the answer is D.

answers.value: Neither statement is true: no process has been provided in the Constitution to enforce the Fundamental Duties, and they are moral and civic obligations rather than correlatives of legal duties
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: Part IVA lays down the Fundamental Duties but the Constitution provides no mechanism for their enforcement, and unlike the Fundamental Rights they are non-justiciable; whether Parliament may legislate to give effect to some of them is a separate question from whether such a process 'has been provided'. Statement 2 is incorrect as commonly understood: the Fundamental Duties are moral and civic obligations addressed to the citizen, not the correlatives of enforceable legal duties. The runner-up is B (2 only), which would win if the examiner had in mind that some duties do have legal counterparts in existing statutes, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 for respecting the National Flag and Anthem, or environmental legislation for the duty to protect the environment - a link the Verma Committee (1999) drew explicitly.

answers.value: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct; Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association, not the Madras Mahajana Sabha
answers.reasoning: Pair 1 is correct: the British Indian Association was founded at Calcutta in 1851 with Raja Radhakanta Deb as its first President and Debendranath Tagore as Secretary. Pair 2 is wrong: Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association in 1852 and the newspaper Crescent; the Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded in 1884 by M. Viraraghavachariar, G. Subramania Iyer and P. Anandacharlu. Pair 3 is correct: the Indian Association was founded at Calcutta in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee along with Anandamohan Bose. Hence 1 and 3 only.

answers.value: Economic liberty is not in the Preamble; the Preamble secures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and economic justice rather than economic liberty
answers.reasoning: The Preamble resolves to secure to all citizens 'JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity'. Liberty is therefore promised in five named forms - thought, expression, belief, faith and worship - which covers options A, C and D. The word 'economic' appears in the Preamble only as a qualifier of justice, never of liberty, so economic liberty is the objective not embodied in it and B is the answer.

answers.value: Both statements are correct: QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and Indian industry, and its Chairman is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendation of industry
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Quality Council of India was established in 1997 as an autonomous body set up jointly by the Government of India and the Indian industry, represented by the three apex chambers ASSOCHAM, CII and FICCI, and it is registered as a society. Statement 2 follows QCI's own description of its governance: the Chairman of QCI is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendation of the industry to the Government, an arrangement that reflects the joint public-private character of the body. The runner-up is A (1 only), which would win if the appointment is in fact made by the administrative ministry (DIPP) rather than the Prime Minister, or if 'on the recommendations of the industry' overstates the industry's formal role - this is the statement a reviewer should verify first.

answers.value: Only 1 and 2: Small Finance Banks exist to supply credit to small business units and to small and marginal farmers; encouraging young rural entrepreneurs is not among their stated objectives
answers.reasoning: The RBI's guidelines state the objectives of Small Finance Banks as furthering financial inclusion by providing savings vehicles to unserved and underserved sections and by supplying credit to small business units, small and marginal farmers, micro and small industries and other unorganised sector entities, through high-technology low-cost operations. Statements 1 and 2 are lifted almost verbatim from that clause and are correct. Statement 3 is not in the objectives: the target group is defined by size and by exclusion from formal credit, not by the borrower's age, and the mandate is not confined to rural areas. The runner-up is D (1, 2 and 3), which would win if the examiner treated 'young entrepreneurs in rural areas' as an acceptable paraphrase of micro and small enterprises in unserved regions rather than as an added condition.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct: the first APMCHUD was held in New Delhi in 2006 on that theme, but India does not host all the conferences and they are not annual
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the first Asia Pacific Ministerial Conference on Housing and Urban Development was hosted by India at New Delhi in December 2006 on the theme of emerging urban forms, policy responses and governance structures. Statement 2 is incorrect on two counts: later conferences were hosted by other countries - Iran (2008), the Republic of Korea (2010), Jordan (2012) and again Korea (2014) - so India does not host them all, and the conferences are held roughly every two years rather than annually. The claimed partnership with ADB, APEC and ASEAN is also not the organising arrangement. Hence A. The reasoning above argues for A and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Democracy's superior virtue is that it calls into activity the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women
answers.reasoning: This is the classic liberal-democratic argument, associated with John Stuart Mill and restated by Harold Laski: the merit of democracy is not that it produces the most expert or the swiftest government, but that participation develops the civic intelligence and moral character of ordinary citizens. Options B, C and D each point the other way - to executive strength, to a heroic individual leader and to party cadres respectively - which are the very concentrations of authority that democratic theory contrasts itself against.

answers.value: UPI makes mobile wallets unnecessary for online payments, since money moves directly between bank accounts
answers.reasoning: The Unified Payments Interface lets a user push or pull funds directly between bank accounts from a smartphone using a virtual payment address, with no need to pre-load money into an intermediary wallet, so option A is the direct and most likely consequence. Option B is speculation about the disappearance of cash that the interface itself cannot deliver. Option C confuses a domestic retail payments rail with foreign investment policy. Option D is wrong because direct benefit transfer already runs on the Aadhaar Payment Bridge and core banking, and does not depend on UPI.

answers.value: These are terms from cosmology and particle physics, used in observing and understanding the Universe
answers.reasoning: An event horizon is the boundary of a black hole beyond which nothing can escape, and a singularity is the point of infinite density at its centre or at the Big Bang; string theory is a candidate framework for unifying gravity with quantum mechanics, and the Standard Model is the established theory of fundamental particles and three of the four forces. All four belong to the physics of the cosmos and its constituents, so they arise in the context of observing and understanding the Universe. They have nothing to do with eclipse geometry, satellite launches or biological evolution.

answers.value: All three uses are valid: genome sequencing identifies markers for disease resistance and drought tolerance, shortens varietal development, and helps decipher host-pathogen relationships
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: sequencing a crop genome allows molecular markers linked to traits such as disease resistance and drought tolerance to be located. Statement 2 is correct: with such markers, marker-assisted selection lets breeders screen seedlings in the laboratory rather than waiting for field expression over successive generations, cutting years off the development of a new variety. Statement 3 is correct: sequencing both the crop and its pathogen reveals the resistance and virulence genes on either side, which is exactly how host-pathogen interactions are dissected. All three are immediate, established applications, so D.

answers.value: The main advantage of a parliamentary system is that the executive remains responsible to the legislature
answers.reasoning: The defining feature and chief merit of the parliamentary form is responsible government: the council of ministers is drawn from and remains collectively answerable to the legislature, which can remove it at any time through a vote of no confidence, so accountability is continuous rather than periodic. The remaining options all describe the presidential form - separation of executive and legislature (A), continuity and efficiency arising from a fixed-term executive (B), and a head of government who can be replaced only at an election (D).

answers.value: Rights and Duties are correlative - every right implies a corresponding duty
answers.reasoning: Rights are claims recognised by society, and a claim is meaningless unless others are under a corresponding obligation to respect it; my right to free speech carries your duty not to silence me, and my right to property carries your duty not to take it. Indian constitutional practice reflects this, with Part III rights sitting alongside the Fundamental Duties added by the Forty-second Amendment. Option B is wrong because rights are conferred and protected by society and cannot be independent of it; options C and D are one-sided assertions that break the correlation the question is testing.

answers.value: The Preamble reflects the mind of the makers of the Constitution
answers.reasoning: The Preamble sets out the source of authority (We, the People of India), the nature of the polity (sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic), the objectives (justice, liberty, equality and fraternity) and the date of adoption, so it states in one place what the framers intended the Constitution to achieve. The Supreme Court has repeatedly described it in these terms, holding in In re Berubari Union that the Preamble is the key to open the mind of the makers. The Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties each express only one part of that design.

answers.value: Seven States - Nagaland, Assam, West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala
answers.reasoning: Leaving Kohima, every road out of Nagaland towards the rest of India passes through Assam, and the only land route from the North East into the Indian mainland is the Siliguri corridor in West Bengal, so the first three States are fixed as Nagaland, Assam and West Bengal. Running south, West Bengal adjoins Odisha, Odisha adjoins Andhra Pradesh, and since Andhra Pradesh does not touch Kerala one southern State must intervene - either Tamil Nadu or Karnataka - before reaching Kerala. That gives a minimum of seven States including origin and destination, so the answer is B.

answers.value: All three - adjournment motion, question hour and supplementary questions - are devices through which Parliament controls the Council of Ministers
answers.reasoning: The adjournment motion sets aside the normal business of the House to debate a definite matter of urgent public importance and carries an element of censure of the government, so it is plainly an instrument of control. Question hour compels ministers to answer for the working of their departments on the floor of the House. Supplementary questions are the follow-ups a member may put after the ministerial reply, and they are often the sharpest part of the exercise because they cannot be prepared for in advance. All three are recognised parliamentary devices of executive accountability, so D.

answers.value: Motupalli was the great seaport of the Kakatiya kingdom
answers.reasoning: Motupalli, on the Andhra coast, was the principal port of the Kakatiyas of Warangal. Ganapatideva issued the celebrated Motupalli Abhaya Shasanam, a charter guaranteeing the safety of foreign merchants and their goods, and Marco Polo describes the port's trade in his account of the region. Machilipatnam (Masulipatnam) rose to prominence later, under the Qutb Shahis and the European companies; Kakinada is a modern port; and Nelluru (Nellore) was an inland administrative and temple town, not a Kakatiya seaport.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the GCCA is an EU initiative giving technical and financial support to targeted developing countries; statement 3 is false, WRI and WBCSD coordinate the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, not the GCCA
answers.reasoning: The Global Climate Change Alliance was launched in 2007 by the European Commission, so statement 1 is correct. Its stated purpose is to help the poorest and most vulnerable developing countries — chiefly Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States — integrate climate change into their development policies and national budgets, through technical assistance and grant finance, so statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 attaches the wrong body: the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development jointly run the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, a corporate emissions-accounting standard, and have no coordinating role in the GCCA.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct — Sautrantika and Sammitiya were Buddhist, not Jain, sects; the Sarvastivadins did hold that phenomena's constituents exist perpetually in latent form
answers.reasoning: Sautrantika and Sammitiya (Sammatiya) both belong to the eighteen early schools of BUDDHISM — the Sautrantikas took the sutras rather than the Abhidharma as authoritative, and the Sammitiyas were a branch of the Pudgalavada tradition — so statement 1 is wrong in assigning them to Jainism. Statement 2 correctly states the defining doctrine of the Sarvastivada, whose very name means 'the theory that all exists': the dharmas constituting phenomena are held to exist in past, present and future, persisting in a latent condition rather than being wholly momentary. That doctrine is precisely what distinguished the Sarvastivadins from the strict momentariness of other schools.

answers.reasoning: Lebanon's entire western frontier is the Mediterranean, and Syria has a Mediterranean coast running from the Turkish border down to Lebanon, including the ports of Latakia and Tartus. answers.value: Both statements are wrong — NIIF is not an organ of NITI Aayog (it is a fund set up by the Ministry of Finance and registered with SEBI as an AIF), and its corpus is of the order of Rs 40,000 crore, not Rs 4,00,000 crore

answers.reasoning: The Global Infrastructure Facility was launched by the World Bank Group as a global collaboration platform. It is neither an ASEAN body financed by the Asian Development Bank (A), nor an OECD-anchored bankers' club (C), nor a UNCTAD-funded programme (D); UNCTAD is a trade and development research and policy body and does not finance infrastructure.

answers.value: A nomination can be filed by any citizen of India who is registered as an elector in a constituency — residence in the particular constituency being contested is not required

A is wrong because mere residence in India is not enough (a non-citizen resident cannot stand), and D is wrong because citizenship alone does not suffice — an unregistered citizen, or one disqualified from the roll, cannot file.

answers.value: Only statement 3 is correct — Pulicat Lake lies in two States (Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu); the Himalayas and the Western Ghats each extend over more than five States
answers.reasoning: The Indian Himalaya runs through far more than five States — Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh at the least, with the eastern ranges continuing into Assam, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram — so the word 'only' in statement 1 defeats it. The Western Ghats, as delimited by the Government of India for Ecologically Sensitive Area purposes and by the Gadgil and Kasturirangan panels, run through six States: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, so 'five only' is also wrong. The whole item pivots on whether Gujarat is counted, and a reviewer should look there first.

answers.value: BOD measures organic pollution load in water — a pollution assay for aquatic ecosystems
answers.reasoning: Biological (Biochemical) Oxygen Demand is the quantity of dissolved oxygen consumed by aerobic micro-organisms while decomposing the organic matter in a water sample, conventionally measured over five days at 20 degrees Celsius. A high BOD means a heavy load of biodegradable organic matter — sewage, food-processing effluent, agricultural runoff — which strips oxygen from the water and asphyxiates fish and other aquatic life. It is therefore a standard index of organic water pollution, and has nothing to do with oxygen in blood, in forests, or at high altitude.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is false because UN-Habitat's partners are not restricted to governments and local authorities
answers.reasoning: UN-Habitat is the UN programme mandated by the General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities with the goal of adequate shelter for all, which is statement 1 almost verbatim. Statement 3 is likewise correct: UN-Habitat's work is tied to the wider UN objective of reducing poverty and improving access to safe drinking water and basic sanitation, and it runs a Water and Sanitation Trust Fund to that end. Statement 2 fails on the word 'only' — UN-Habitat works with a wide partner base that includes non-governmental organisations, community and grassroots groups, professional and research institutions, the private sector and other UN agencies, not just governments and municipal authorities.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct — NSQF explicitly recognises informal and non-formal learning through Recognition of Prior Learning, but it does aim at mobility between vocational and general education
answers.reasoning: The National Skills Qualification Framework organises qualifications into levels defined by learning outcomes rather than by how the learning was acquired, and it provides for Recognition of Prior Learning so that competence gained informally on the job can be assessed and certified. Statement 1's 'only through formal learning' therefore inverts one of the framework's central features. Statement 2 is a stated objective of the NSQF: by making qualifications comparable and outcome-based it enables horizontal and vertical movement between the vocational stream and general education, so that a vocational qualification is no longer a dead end.

answers.value: Dyarchy meant splitting the provincial subjects into two categories — 'transferred' subjects administered by ministers responsible to the legislature, and 'reserved' subjects retained by the Governor and his executive council
answers.reasoning: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces by the Government of India Act, 1919 (the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms). Subjects were first divided between the Centre and the provinces, and then the provincial list was itself split in two: transferred subjects such as education, local self-government, public health and agriculture were placed under Indian ministers answerable to the legislative council, while reserved subjects such as police, land revenue, justice and irrigation stayed with the Governor acting with his executive council. Option A describes bicameralism, which the 1919 Act also introduced at the Centre but which is a separate feature; B describes federal division of powers; C describes the Home Government-Government of India relationship, not dyarchy.

answers.value: Both statements are wrong — the National Career Service is a Ministry of Labour and Employment initiative, not DoPT's, and it serves all jobseekers rather than being aimed at 'uneducated youth'
answers.reasoning: The National Career Service was launched in 2015 as a mission-mode project of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, which transformed the old National Employment Service and its employment exchanges into an online portal linking jobseekers, employers, skill providers, counsellors and placement organisations. The Department of Personnel and Training is concerned with civil-service personnel policy and recruitment to government posts, so statement 1 misattributes the scheme. Statement 2 is right that the launch was in mission mode but wrong in its target: the NCS is open to jobseekers across the educational spectrum, including graduates and skilled workers, and is not a scheme confined to uneducated youth.

answers.value: S4A is an RBI scheme for reworking the financial structure — splitting sustainable from unsustainable debt — of large corporate borrowers in genuine difficulty
answers.reasoning: The Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets was issued by the Reserve Bank of India in June 2016 to deal with large stressed corporate accounts. Under it, an independent agency determines how much of the borrower's debt can be serviced from existing cash flows; that 'sustainable' portion is retained as debt on existing terms, while the unsustainable remainder is converted into equity or equity-like instruments held by the lenders. It is thus a bank-regulatory restructuring tool, not an environmental costing procedure (A), not a disinvestment plan for public sector undertakings (C), and not a provision of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (D), which is a separate statutory resolution framework administered through the NCLT.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct — the CCAC is a UNEP-hosted voluntary partnership, not a G20 initiative, but it does target methane, black carbon and HFCs
answers.reasoning: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition was launched in 2012 by the United Nations Environment Programme together with six founding countries (Bangladesh, Canada, Ghana, Mexico, Sweden and the United States) and has since grown into a broad voluntary partnership of states, intergovernmental bodies and civil-society organisations; it is not an initiative of the G20, so statement 1 is wrong. Statement 2 is correct: the Coalition's mandate is short-lived climate pollutants, and its priority pollutants are black carbon, methane and hydrofluorocarbons, along with tropospheric ozone, all of which have short atmospheric lifetimes so that cutting them yields quick climate and air-quality benefits.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct — the IOD is defined by the temperature contrast between the tropical WESTERN and tropical EASTERN INDIAN Ocean, not the eastern Pacific, but it can indeed modulate El Nino's effect on the monsoon
answers.reasoning: The Indian Ocean Dipole is measured as the difference in sea surface temperature between the western equatorial Indian Ocean (off East Africa, the Arabian Sea sector) and the south-eastern equatorial Indian Ocean (off Sumatra and Java). Statement 1 replaces the eastern Indian Ocean pole with the tropical eastern Pacific, which is the domain of El Nino and a different phenomenon altogether, so it is wrong as printed. Statement 2 is correct and is why the IOD is watched during monsoon forecasting: a strongly positive IOD warms the western Indian Ocean and enhances moisture convergence over India, and has repeatedly been observed to offset or mask the rainfall deficit that an El Nino year would otherwise produce.

answers.value: The Chambal River (National Chambal Sanctuary) is the best place to see gharials in the wild
answers.reasoning: The gharial is a fish-eating, narrow-snouted crocodilian of clear, fast-flowing rivers with deep pools and sandbanks for basking and nesting. The National Chambal Sanctuary, on the Chambal across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, holds by far the largest surviving breeding population and is the mainstay of gharial conservation in India. Bhitarkanika's mangrove creeks are saltwater crocodile habitat, Pulicat is a brackish coastal lagoon known for flamingos and other waterbirds, and Deepor Beel is a freshwater wetland in Assam noted for migratory birds — none of them is gharial country.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct — IONS is a voluntary maritime-cooperation initiative of Indian Ocean littoral navies, but its inaugural edition was in 2008, not 2015
answers.reasoning: The Indian Ocean Naval Symposium was conceived by the Indian Navy and its inaugural gathering was held at New Delhi in February 2008, with India holding the first chairmanship; by 2015 the chair had passed on through the UAE and South Africa to Australia. Statement 1's date is therefore wrong, even though it correctly names India and the Indian Navy for the inaugural edition. Statement 2 accurately describes the forum: it is a voluntary, consultative initiative bringing together the navies of the littoral states of the Indian Ocean Region to increase maritime cooperation, share information and build common understanding on regional maritime security.

answers.value: The Bodhisattva Padmapani painting is at Ajanta
answers.reasoning: The Padmapani — the bodhisattva holding a blue lotus, painted with downcast eyes and a serene, inward expression — occupies the wall beside the shrine antechamber of Cave 1 at Ajanta, paired with the Bodhisattva Vajrapani, and is the single most reproduced image of Indian mural painting. Ellora and Badami are renowned for rock-cut sculpture and architecture rather than for this mural; Bagh (Madhya Pradesh) does have important Buddhist paintings closely related in style to Ajanta's, but the Padmapani is an Ajanta work.

answers.value: Only pair 1 is correct — Chaliha Sahib is a Sindhi festival; Nanda Raj Jaat is an Uttarakhand (Garhwal-Kumaon) pilgrimage, not Gond, and Wari-Warkari is Maharashtrian, not Santhal
answers.reasoning: Chaliha Sahib is the forty-day observance kept by the Sindhi community in devotion to Jhulelal, the community's water deity, so pair 1 is correctly matched. The Nanda Devi Raj Jat is a Himalayan pilgrimage held roughly once in twelve years in Uttarakhand, in which the image of the goddess Nanda is carried in procession from Nauti up to Homkund; it belongs to the Garhwali and Kumaoni hill communities, not to the Gonds of central India. The Wari is the annual foot-pilgrimage of the Warkari sect of Maharashtra, who carry the padukas of Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram to Pandharpur on Ashadhi Ekadashi; it has no connection with the Santhals, an Adivasi people of Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.

answers.value: All three practices can help conserve water — zero tillage and retained crop residue both cut evaporation and runoff, and gypsum applied before irrigation improves infiltration in sodic, crust-forming soils
answers.reasoning: Reduced or zero tillage leaves the soil undisturbed, preserving pore structure and the surface mulch, which lowers evaporative loss and improves the soil's capacity to take in and hold water, so practice 1 helps. Leaving crop residue in the field works the same way from the surface: the residue shades the soil, reduces direct evaporation, slows runoff and improves infiltration, so practice 3 helps. Practice 2 is the judgement call: gypsum is best known as an amendment for sodic and alkali soils, where its calcium displaces exchangeable sodium, flocculates dispersed clay and breaks up the surface crust; applied before irrigation this raises the infiltration rate so that water enters the root zone instead of ponding and running off, which is a genuine gain in irrigation water-use efficiency. Since the stem asks only what 'can help' in water conservation, all three qualify. RUNNER-UP: C (1 and 3 only) — it wins if gypsum is read strictly as a soil-reclamation chemical whose purpose is removing sodium rather than saving water, and indeed the leaching that follows gypsum application on sodic land consumes extra water rather than saving it. The item turns entirely on how permissively 'can help in water conservation' is read for statement 2. [Answer corrected to C from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached D. The reasoning above argues for D and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Only statement 3 is correct — the Soil Health Card aims at balanced, judicious fertilizer use; it has nothing to do with expanding irrigated area or with bank loan assessment
answers.reasoning: The Soil Health Card Scheme tests farmers' soil for its macro- and micro-nutrient status, pH, organic carbon and other parameters, and issues a card carrying crop-wise recommendations on the nutrients and fertilizers actually needed. Its purpose is to correct the indiscriminate and unbalanced application of fertilizers — especially excess urea — so statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 belongs to a different scheme: expanding the area under assured irrigation is the objective of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana. Statement 2 is simply not part of the scheme's design; the card is an agronomic advisory to the farmer, and quantum of crop credit is fixed by the scale of finance for the crop and the land held, not by soil quality.

answers.value: All three pairs are correctly matched — lead in lipstick, brominated vegetable oil in soft drinks, and monosodium glutamate in Chinese fast food
answers.reasoning: Lead has repeatedly been detected as a contaminant in lipsticks, entering through the mineral pigments used to colour them, and regulators have had to set permissible limits — a well-known consumer-safety controversy. Brominated vegetable oil is a vegetable oil bonded with bromine and used as an emulsifier to keep citrus flavouring evenly dispersed in soft drinks; it is contentious because of bromine accumulation in body tissue and has been restricted or banned in several countries. Monosodium glutamate is the flavour enhancer characteristically associated with Chinese fast food, long debated under the label 'Chinese restaurant syndrome'. All three associations are exactly the unwanted or controversial chemicals the question describes.

answers.value: All three are genuine OLED advantages over LCDs — fabrication on flexible plastic substrates, roll-up displays that can be embedded in clothing, and transparent displays
answers.reasoning: An OLED is an emissive device: each pixel is a thin organic film that generates its own light, so the display needs no glass backlight assembly, no diffuser and no rigid liquid-crystal cell. The organic layers can be deposited on thin plastic film, which makes flexible substrates possible (statement 1) and in turn makes bendable and roll-up panels light and robust enough to be built into fabric and clothing (statement 2). Because the emissive stack can be made from very thin layers with transparent electrodes, an OLED panel can be substantially see-through when switched off, giving transparent displays (statement 3) — something an LCD cannot readily do since it depends on a backlight and polarisers behind the panel.

answers.value: Only Arasavalli is famous for a Sun temple; Amarakantak is a Narmada-source pilgrimage centre and Omkareshwar is a Shiva Jyotirlinga site
answers.reasoning: Arasavalli, near Srikakulam in Andhra Pradesh, has the Suryanarayana Swamy temple, one of the very few functioning Sun temples in India and celebrated for the alignment that lets the sun's rays fall on the deity at certain times of the year. Amarakantak in Madhya Pradesh, on the Maikal range, is revered as the source of the Narmada and is associated with Narmada and Shiva shrines, not with surya worship. Omkareshwar, on an island in the Narmada, houses one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and is likewise a Shaiva centre. So only pair 1 answers the stem.

answers.value: Neither statement is correct: Indian elections use first-past-the-post with no 50% threshold, and the Constitution nowhere allots the Speaker's post to the majority party or the Deputy Speaker's to the Opposition
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: India uses the first-past-the-post (simple plurality) system, in which the candidate polling the largest number of votes wins regardless of whether that is a majority — there is no 50% requirement anywhere in the law. Statement 2 is wrong because it attributes to the Constitution something the Constitution does not say: Article 93 merely requires the Lok Sabha to choose two of its members as Speaker and Deputy Speaker, and the practice of leaving the Deputy Speaker's post to the Opposition is a political convention, not a constitutional provision. With both statements false, the answer is 'Neither 1 nor 2'.

answers.value: Statements 2, 3 and 4 occurred after 1991 (rising share of world trade, rising FDI inflows, sharply higher forex reserves); the share of agriculture in GDP fell rather than rose
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is the odd one out and is false in the opposite direction: agriculture's share of GDP has fallen steadily through the post-liberalisation period, from roughly 30 percent in 1991 to under 18 percent, as services expanded. Statement 2 is correct — India's share of world merchandise exports rose from about 0.5 percent in 1991 to roughly 1.7 percent. Statement 3 is correct: FDI inflows, negligible before 1991, rose to tens of billions of dollars a year. Statement 4 is correct and is the most dramatic of the four — foreign exchange reserves went from about USD 1 billion at the 1991 crisis to over USD 350 billion. So 2, 3 and 4 only.

answers.value: Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer is the technique used for reproductive cloning of animals
answers.reasoning: In SCNT the nucleus of an ordinary body (somatic) cell is transferred into an enucleated egg cell; the reconstructed egg is stimulated to divide and, if implanted, develops into an animal genetically identical to the nucleus donor. This is exactly how Dolly the sheep was produced, and it is the standard route to reproductive cloning of animals. Biolarvicides (A) come from microbial agents such as Bacillus thuringiensis, biodegradable plastics (B) from microbial polymers such as PHB, and disease-free organisms (D) from tissue culture or genetic modification — none of these uses nuclear transfer.

answers.value: Both are correct: NPCI's mandate expressly includes promoting financial inclusion, and RuPay is NPCI's own card payment scheme
answers.reasoning: NPCI was set up as the umbrella organisation for retail payments in India, with the stated objective of building an affordable payment infrastructure that reaches the common man — so statement 1 is correct, and its products (RuPay, AePS, BHIM/UPI, the Jan Dhan card ecosystem) are precisely financial-inclusion instruments. Statement 2 is correct as a plain fact: RuPay, India's indigenous card payment network launched as an alternative to Visa and Mastercard, is an NPCI product. Both being true, the answer is 'Both 1 and 2'.

answers.value: M-STrIPES is the monitoring and patrolling software used in tiger reserves — Monitoring System for Tigers: Intensive Protection and Ecological Status
answers.reasoning: M-STrIPES stands for Monitoring System for Tigers — Intensive Protection and Ecological Status, an app-based system developed by the National Tiger Conservation Authority. Forest patrol teams use it to log GPS tracks, sightings, signs and evidence of poaching, which is then analysed to assess protection effort and tiger habitat status. It is therefore a tool of tiger-reserve management, not a captive-breeding programme (A), a navigation system (C — that is NavIC/IRNSS) or a highway security scheme (D).

answers.value: Only statement 1 is a likely advantage — GST subsumes multiple taxes levied by multiple authorities and creates a single national market; the claims about the Current Account Deficit and about overtaking China are not consequences of GST
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is the core rationale for GST: it replaced a thicket of central and state indirect taxes (excise, service tax, VAT, octroi, entry tax, CST) with one tax, removing the cascading effect and inter-state tax barriers so that India functions as a single market. Statement 2 is wrong because GST is a domestic indirect tax on consumption; the Current Account Deficit is determined by trade in goods and services and external flows, and nothing in GST 'drastically reduces' it. Statement 3 is wrong on its face — no single tax reform enormously increases the size of an economy or lets it overtake an economy several times larger 'in the near future'. Note the stem's giveaway adverbs, 'drastically' and 'enormously': both flag overreach.

answers.value: The Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement is the free trade agreement being negotiated between India and the European Union
answers.reasoning: The BTIA is the formal name of the India–EU free trade agreement, negotiations for which were launched in 2007 and which covers goods, services, investment and government procurement. India's engagements with the other three bodies are named differently: with the GCC it is a separate framework agreement, the OECD is a policy think-tank rather than a trade-negotiating bloc India signs FTAs with, and the SCO is a security and political grouping without a bilateral trade agreement of this name.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — India ratified the TFA in April 2016 and the TFA emerged from the Bali Ministerial Package of December 2013 — but the TFA entered into force in February 2017, not January 2016
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: India deposited its instrument of acceptance of the Trade Facilitation Agreement in April 2016. answers.value: Chabahar gives India a sea route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan, removing its dependence on Pakistani transit
answers.reasoning: Pakistan has denied India overland transit to Afghanistan, so Chabahar on Iran's Makran coast — just outside the Strait of Hormuz and connected onward by the Zaranj–Delaram road and planned rail links — is India's alternative corridor to Afghanistan and, through Iran, to Central Asia and the INSTC. That strategic bypass is the whole point of the project. Option A is wrong because Chabahar faces the Arabian Sea toward Central Asia, not Africa; B misstates the purpose, since Iran is not an Arab country and the port is about connectivity, not Arab ties; D is wrong on both counts, as Pakistan is precisely the country being bypassed and no such Iraq–India pipeline is involved.

answers.value: All three — service providers, data centres and body corporate — are under a legal obligation to report cyber security incidents to CERT-In
answers.reasoning: Reporting is governed by the CERT-In Rules framed under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act. The rules draw a deliberate distinction: any individual or affected entity generally *may* report an incident, but service providers, intermediaries, data centres and body corporate *shall* report specified cyber security incidents to CERT-In within a reasonable time. Since all three categories named in the item fall on the mandatory side of that line, the answer includes 1, 2 and 3.

answers.value: The right to vote and to contest an election is a legal (statutory) right — created and regulated by the Representation of the People Act, not a fundamental, natural or purely constitutional right
answers.reasoning: The settled judicial position, from N. P. Ponnuswami onwards and repeated in Jyoti Basu and Kuldip Nayar, is that the right to vote or to stand as a candidate is not a civil or common-law right but 'a creature of statute', subject to the limitations that statute imposes; the actual entitlement to vote is conferred by Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and eligibility to contest by the same Act. Article 326 does not itself confer a right to vote — it entitles an adult citizen to be *registered* as a voter, and even that is made subject to any law made by the appropriate legislature. It is clearly not a fundamental right (it is outside Part III) and not a natural right (it exists only where the state creates elections). RUNNER-UP: (C) Constitutional Right — this wins if the setter treats Article 326 as directly conferring the franchise, which is how some polity texts describe it while using 'constitutional right' and 'legal right' almost interchangeably for rights outside Part III. What tips the item toward 'legal' is that the stem yokes voting to *being elected*: no provision of the Constitution confers a right to contest, so the only classification that covers both halves of the stem is the statutory one. [Answer corrected to C from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached D. The reasoning above argues for D and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: eLISA is a space-based interferometer designed to detect gravitational waves

Being in space and having arms far longer than any ground detector, it targets low-frequency gravitational waves that LIGO-type instruments cannot reach. Neutrino detection (A) uses very different underground detectors such as large water-Cherenkov or liquid-scintillator tanks, and options C and D describe defence and space-weather work unrelated to interferometry.

answers.value: Schedule I listing means the species gets the highest degree of statutory protection under the Act — the same level the tiger enjoys
answers.reasoning: Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is the highest protection category: hunting is prohibited throughout India and offences attract the most stringent penalties, with only narrow exceptions permitted at the highest level of authority. The tiger is a Schedule I species, so a tortoise placed in the same Schedule receives the same statutory protection — option A. Option B is wrong because Schedule I says nothing about a species being extinct in the wild; listing is a legal protection status, not a statement that conservation has already failed. Option C is wrong because the Schedules do not classify species by endemism — Schedule I includes widely distributed species. Since B and C are both false, D falls with them.

answers.value: Judicial Review is the judiciary's power to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders and to declare them void if they violate the Constitution
answers.reasoning: Judicial review is the power of the Supreme Court and the High Courts to test laws and executive actions against the Constitution and strike down anything repugnant to it; it flows from Articles 13, 32 and 226 and has been held part of the basic structure. Option B is a well-known limit rather than the definition — courts examine the constitutional validity of a law, never the wisdom or policy merit behind it, which is for the legislature. Option C describes a pre-enactment scrutiny that does not exist in India, where review is post-enactment (the President may seek an advisory opinion under Article 143, but that is a distinct power). Option D describes the review of the Court's own judgments under Article 137, which is 'review' in a different, narrower sense.

answers.value: The proposed second home for the Gir lions is Kuno Palpur Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh
answers.reasoning: Because the entire wild population of the Asiatic lion is confined to the Gir landscape in Gujarat, a single epidemic or catastrophe could wipe it out, so a second free-ranging population was proposed at Kuno Palpur in Madhya Pradesh, a site prepared for the purpose with villages relocated and prey base built up; the Supreme Court in 2013 directed the translocation. Corbett and Sariska are tiger habitats in the Himalayan foothills and the Aravallis respectively, and Mudumalai in the Nilgiris is likewise a tiger and elephant landscape — none was the identified lion site.

answers.value: Dissolution of the Legislative Assembly and dissolution of local bodies are not necessary consequences of President's rule; dismissal of the State Council of Ministers is
answers.reasoning: The question asks which effects do *not* necessarily follow. Statement 1 qualifies: on a proclamation under Article 356 the President may either dissolve the Assembly or merely keep it in suspended animation, so dissolution is an option, not a necessity. Statement 3 qualifies even more clearly: President's rule operates on the State government; panchayats and municipalities, which are constitutional bodies under Parts IX and IX-A with their own five-year terms, are not dissolved by it. Statement 2 does not qualify — the very effect of the proclamation is that the President assumes the functions of the State government, so the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister is invariably dismissed. Hence 1 and 3 only.

answers.value: The Right against Exploitation covers only prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour (Article 23) and prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines (Article 24)
answers.reasoning: The Right against Exploitation consists of exactly two Articles. Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour, which is statement 1. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below fourteen in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment, which is statement 4. Statement 2, abolition of untouchability, is Article 17 and belongs to the Right to Equality. Statement 3, protection of the interests of minorities, is Article 29 and belongs to the Cultural and Educational Rights. So only 1 and 4.

answers.value: Sumatra — the northern tip of Sumatra lies only about 150 km from Great Nicobar across the Great Channel, far nearer than Borneo, Java or Sri Lanka
answers.reasoning: Great Nicobar is the southernmost island of the Nicobar group, and Indira Point at its tip is India's southernmost land. It is separated from Aceh, at the northern end of Sumatra, by the Great Channel, a gap of roughly 150 kilometres — the shortest distance from these islands to any foreign landmass. Java lies far to the south-east beyond Sumatra, Borneo further east again across the Java Sea, and Sri Lanka is over a thousand kilometres away to the west across the Bay of Bengal.

answers.value: The Cabinet system rests on collective responsibility — the Council of Ministers stands or falls together and is answerable, through the popularly elected House, to the people
answers.reasoning: The defining principle of Cabinet government is collective responsibility: ministers deliberate freely in private but are bound to a single public position, and the Council of Ministers as a body must retain the confidence of the popularly elected House, resigning together if it is lost. Article 75(3) states this for India, making the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, which is the people's chamber — hence option C's phrasing of responsibility 'to the people' through parliamentary democracy. The other three options describe motives rather than principles and are all inverted: the Cabinet system exists to concentrate rather than deflect responsibility, so A is wrong; administrative speed (B) is a possible by-product, not the principle; and D reverses the logic, since the Cabinet constrains the head of government rather than propping him up.

answers.value: Indian federalism is not the result of an agreement among the federating units — the Union was created by the Constitution, states cannot secede, and the federation is 'indestructible'
answers.reasoning: Unlike the American federation, which was formed by an agreement among previously sovereign states that came together, the Indian Union was not created by any compact among its units; the Constituent Assembly created the Union and then distributed territory into states, and Parliament can under Article 3 alter their boundaries, names and very existence without their consent. Ambedkar put it that the Union is indestructible though the states are not, and that no state has a right to secede. So option D is the statement that is *not* a feature of Indian federalism. The other three are true of India: an integrated independent judiciary (A), a division of powers through the three Lists of the Seventh Schedule (B), and Rajya Sabha seats allotted broadly in proportion to population rather than equally (C) — the last being a genuine, if distinguishing, feature of the Indian scheme rather than something absent from it.
